newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel a tad firmer along with IP.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel a tad firmer along with IP.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices were marginally firmer on Wednesday along with higher gas oil and crude futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE), traders said.
Swaps gas oil for March and April rose by 15 cents per barrel as IPE last traded $1.00 a tonne higher at $176.00.
But traders remained jittery on talk that several Western and MidEast traders were mulling to ship in gas oil cargoes from Western Europe to this region during end March or early April.
They noted that none of these cargoes have been fixed yet as the region enters a period of low demand.
They said if these arbitrage cargoes did arrive here, it would fill in the supply gap caused by the shutdown of Mobil Oil Singapore's 280,000-barrel-per-day refinery for one month from March 15.

Traders said despite talk of enquiries for gas oil from China, no purchases have been seen so far this week. They said China was still hoping for prices to dip to at least $200 per tonne, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) southern China basis, but sellers were seeking $206-$207 levels.
Demand has emerged from Sri Lanka which issued another purchase tender for March 9-10 delivery for 220,000 barrels of gas oil and 55,000 barrels of jet fuel. The tender closes on February 25.

Taiwan's gas oil sale tender for March 1-12 lifting fob attracted only five offers, reflecting current soft demand for the product. The offers ranged between $25.50-$26.00 a barrel, lower than the $29.50 which was awarded in the last tender for January 26-February 15 lifting fob.
Taiwan might sell two cargoes if the offer price was deemed attractive.

Physical gas oil was offered slightly higher on Wednesday with 150,000 barrels lifting March 16-20 at $25.45, down from Tuesday's $25.70. A bid for 200,000 barrels lifting March 6-10 was seen at $25.45 a barrel, up from Tuesday's $25.20.
